Kesha has gone raw vegan and spends every lunch lecturing about the evils of cooked buckwheat. Your buckwheat is getting cold.
The next department is loudly celebrating a birthday at 9:30 a.m., with candles and group singing. Your stand-up is right through the wall.
left: Ask them to keep it down

text: Sveta is begging you to come along on her blind date “as backup.” You'd sit at the next table.
Two coworkers haven't spoken in a week and pass messages through you. Here comes the third one.
left: Pass it on word for word

text: Someone posted a poll in the team chat: “Who took my cat mug?” Your mug also has a cat. They're identical.
8:00 a.m. The organizer writes: “We forgot to buy the boss's gift! Who lives near the mall?” That's you.
Lev is bragging about his new step-counting watch and demanding the whole team compete with him. You in?
Tanya suggests stopping by the mall after work to pick a gift for your boss. It'll take “half an hour.” Experience says three.
QA has filed bug number fifteen against you, including “the button looks kind of sad.” Reply in the tracker?
The soccer crew needs a player for tonight's match against Accounting. The last time you ran was in high school. Take the field?
Intern Philip brought his résumé and asks you to look it over. He's applying to another company. Help him?
Your neighbor left a banana peel on his desk overnight. By Monday it'll be a surprise. Clean up after him?
Irina is back from vacation, showing everyone 400 beach photos. You're on number forty. She promises “the best ones are at the end.”
The “Sweets Table” chat announced: anyone who's late brings pastries. You were two minutes late. Give up?
Zhenya confesses he's quitting tomorrow and hasn't told anyone. The boss asks you why Zhenya is acting so weird.
The security guard at the entrance says your coworker asked him to tell you he borrowed your umbrella “for a bit.” It's pouring outside.
Vlad CCs you on all his emails “to look more serious.” Today three people have already asked you about his projects.
New guy Sasha asks if it's true everyone has to sing an original song at the holiday party. Someone pranked him.
Nurlan is sharing lunch: his mom sent pilaf for the whole floor. The portion is huge, and you have an important meeting after lunch.
Olya put tomato seedlings on the shared windowsill. Now there's not even room for a mug. The tomatoes bring joy only to her.
Coworkers started a book club. This week: a 900-page novel, discussion on Friday. You've read the cover.
The quality team is auditing “workplace culture” and photographing your desk. It holds three mugs and a cactus in a tiny hat.
New guy Vova asks who he can complain to about the noise in the open space. The main source of noise is your best work friend.
left: Send him to the office manager

text: Dina invites you to her watercolor show at a café. Free entry, and the paintings are about the office: one clearly shows the back of your head.
The “Team Council” is picking who'll make the holiday bulletin board. The loudest voice writes: “I nominate whoever's quiet.” That's you.
Your neighbors decided to quit sugar together and hid your candy “for the greater good.” Without candy, the morning feels gray.
Ahmed asks you to cover for him on a client call while he's at the dentist. The client only knows his voice and manner.
The New Year's party. You've unexpectedly been named employee of the year. You need to give a speech thanking your coworkers. Ready?
Tonya is going on maternity leave and handing her work over to you. Her folder is called “Stuff, sort later.”
right: Ask her to walk you through it

text: Intern Julia did your task better than you. The boss noticed and asks who did it.
You sent a voice message to the team chat instead of your friend: “I'm so sick of these people.” Twelve listens.
Rustam offers to carpool: he has a car, and your place is on his way. The catch: he only listens to opera.
A partner team needs data urgently, but they message every three minutes: “Well?” Twenty messages in an hour.
Kristina suggests signing up together for the company's Spanish classes. Classes are at 7 p.m., with lots of homework.
left: Sign up to keep her company

text: The “Wellness” chat announced morning stretching at 9:15 in the conference room. While you think it over, coworkers are rolling out mats.
Vika asks how much you make. It's “just for statistics,” and she also happens to be your boss's best friend.
Renovations have started at the next desk: they're repainting the wall. Paint fumes, workers in newspaper hats. Move over to your coworkers?
Galina invites you to her country house for the harvest: “Just help dig, then barbecue.” She has a third of an acre.
Someone in the team chat is counting how many times the boss said “literally” in the meeting. It's at 47. You were counting too.
Intern Gosha listed you in his internship report as a “legendary mentor.” The report is going to his university.
right: Ask him to drop the adjectives

text: Petya made a mistake, but the boss is chewing you out, mixing up names. Petya sits behind you, silently eating yogurt.
At the holiday party, you're running the raffle. A slip with your name is sticking out of the hat. Prizes: a vacation trip and a frying pan.
right: Give the prize to a coworker

text: Zakhar showed up in the same shirt as you. The whole team thinks you planned it. The photo is already in the chat.
Instead of the promised chair, Purchasing delivered a stool: “We're out of chairs.” Your neighbor already claimed it as a footrest.
right: Give the stool to your neighbor

text: Nika is planning a surprise for the boss and asks you to keep him in his office for twenty minutes. He's heading home.
All morning the “Friday” chat has been picking a movie for tonight in the conference room. Your pick got laughed at. Fight for it?
Said has been late three days in a row and brings you coffee “for your silence.” Today he brought two.
Your neighbor asks you to water his ficus over the weekend. That means coming in on Saturday. The ficus looks like it's pleading.
The partner team rolled out an update, and a week of your work vanished. In their chat they write: “Well, it happens.”
Maya tells you in secret that layoffs are coming. She heard it from the cleaning lady. The cleaning lady always knows everything.
Oleg invites you to his rock band's gig at a basement club. It starts at 10 p.m., and tomorrow's stand-up is at nine.
Two coworkers broke up, and now they demand different AC settings. You sit exactly in the middle.
Rimma is handing out photocopies of her cake recipe “so everyone can try it at home.” You got the last copy.
New hire Alla redesigned the shared report template “to make it prettier.” Now half the team can't find the old buttons.
right: Ask her to change it back

text: Boris won a vacation package in a company contest and offers to sell it to you at half price. It leaves in two days.
Couriers delivered someone else's package to you by mistake: a box of chocolates labeled “To my beloved Natasha.” There are three Natashas in the office.
All week Timofey has been pretending to be busy while quietly passing his work to you. Now he's brought another “small” task.
left: Take it and just do it

text: The party chat asks who's willing to stay till the end and clean up the hall. Everyone writes “I would, but…” You haven't answered yet.
Kamila brought her puppy to work because no one could watch it. It's chewing your shoelaces and looks unbelievably cute.
right: Ask her to take it away

text: In the unofficial chat, people are saying someone got the biggest bonus. Everyone's looking at you. You really did get the most.
Vera is talking you into dance class after work: “Someone from Marketing will be there.” You can't dance.
The next department wants to borrow your conference room “for literally five minutes.” Last time they stayed until lunch.
Rita found an anonymous note with a heart in her bag and wants help figuring out who sent it. The handwriting looks like your boss's.
On his last day, intern Vitya is throwing a farewell party. Everyone's invited, but you have to get up early tomorrow.
Elena once again “borrows” your charger and forgets to return it. Your phone is now at one percent.
Every Monday Gera recounts his athletic feats. Today he ran a marathon and demands applause.
The New Year chat is picking who'll play Santa at the holiday party for employees' kids. They're out of options. You're what's left.
Dima asked you to check his email to a client. It has three typos and an accidental “xoxo.” It goes out in a minute.
At 9:30 a.m., Lyusya brings the team horoscope for discussion. Today your sign is promised “conflict with coworkers.”
Felix offers a trade: he'll go to the boring morning huddle for you, and you'll take his evening call with a contractor.
The team chipped in for coffee machine pods. Your share ran out yesterday, but the pods didn't. Make yourself a cup?
Intern Arina showed up in a snow-white suit, and today you're moving the archive. About forty boxes. Ask her to help?
Yana brought fridge magnets back from vacation for the whole team. Yours says “World's Best Accountant.” You're not an accountant.
New guy Emil doesn't know where to get water, paper, or the conference room key. He's looking at you with kitten eyes. Give him a tour?
At 9:40 a.m., Polina dozed off at her desk, head on the keyboard. Her document already has three pages of the letter “j.” Wake her?
right: Snap a photo for the chat

text: Every morning your row neighbor cracks his neck loudly. Today he offers to “show you the technique.”
Since 7:30 a.m., the team chat has been sharing news links. You overslept and have no idea what everyone's talking about. Admit it?
Nestor suggests “shortening the meeting” by ditching the morning stand-up for a café: “Nobody will notice.” They'll definitely notice you.
8:15 a.m. Someone writes: “Whoever's in first, turn on the kettle.” You're already here, but you don't want to become the kettle person.
Tina puts her vase of flowers on your desk: “It doesn't fit on mine.” That's the third vase this week.
Right at the door, Yura offers you his second breakfast: crêpes with jam. You've been on a diet since Monday, and it's Tuesday.
The guard asks you to personally confirm the new guy is your coworker. You've never seen him before, but he's smiling.
Vika asks if you want to sit by the window together. Sun, a view, and a draft. Your desk is in a quiet corner.
A “Latecomers” chat was created: whoever posts first buys everyone coffee. You're running ten minutes late.
Borya suggests spending the morning break in the massage chair on the first floor. The sign-up sheet is full until lunch.
Coworkers are ordering lunch to the office, and you got stuck taking orders. Five minutes in: twenty-three items and two arguments.
Ulyana whispers for help with her laptop: it's “frozen forever.” In ten minutes she's presenting to a client.
Senya invites you to lunch in the park: “Sun, birds, freedom.” Your task is on fire.
Analytics asks where the “117%” in your report came from. You honestly don't remember.
Mira asks you to sit in on an intern interview for her: “You read people better.” You happen to have a free hour.
Your neighbor proposes a 20-minute quiet hour: lights off in the corner and a nap. He brought a pillow and a sleep mask.
Intern Lyova asks if he can leave early for his grandma's birthday. For some reason, it's your call.
Raya shows photos of her kids' school pageant and asks you to guess which snowflake is her daughter. There are twelve snowflakes.
Coworkers from the sports chat invite you on a lunchtime walk around the block. “Ten thousand steps and back to work.”
Arkady borrows your chair “for a sec” while you're in the kitchen. When you get back, he's sitting on it at the other end of the floor.
A partner team invites you to their presentation: “There'll be pizza.” The topic: optimizing paper clip procurement. Go for the pizza?
Klava thinks you breathe too loudly. She's put on headphones and is staring at you pointedly. How do you react?
Your row neighbor complains the office is freezing and suggests going to the cafeteria for hot tea “for half an hour.”
New guy Nikita accidentally hit Reply All with a question about his salary. He's horrified. Help him survive the shame?
Sabina brings meatballs to work and offers to trade one for your chocolate bar. The meatballs smell divine.
Ostap invites you to the sauna after work: “All of Accounting will be there, we'll network.” You have an early train tomorrow.
At 6:30 p.m., board games start in the conference room. Tonight it's a spy game, and everyone's already hunting the traitor. Stay?
Lilya suggests walking to the subway together through the park. It's twenty minutes longer, but there are squirrels.
Your neighbor is leaving, but you're still working. He offers to leave you his desk lamp and blanket. The blanket is suspiciously soft.
Dessert is served at the holiday party, and you've been chosen as the “secret taster” for a contest. Seven cakes, and you're already stuffed.
Elya asks whether she should leave for another company. You're her only ally on the team.
The team is going to karaoke to celebrate shipping the project. You're tired, but without you there's no one for the love duet.
Slava is staying late, quietly crying over a report. You should have gone home long ago.
7:10 p.m. Rustem wants you to teach him Turkish coffee on the office hot plate: “I want to impress Lena from Marketing.” The smoke detector is right above it.
Regina offers you her fancy weekend spa package since she can't go. It's only half price.
At 6:40 p.m., you see Dmitry from Accounting shyly giving flowers to a new hire. She looks at you: “Help!”
Zhanna offers you a ride home. But on the way she needs to stop by the hardware store “for five minutes.”
The runners invite you for a 7 p.m. jog along the river. “Slow, conversational pace.” You remember their “slow.”
At 6:15 p.m., Tosha asks you to help move his desk to the window. It's solid oak and weighs as much as a piano.
Intern Lera asks you to walk her to the bus stop: “There's a dark alley.” You're going the other way.
7:00 p.m. The chat is collecting for a gift for Sasha, the courier who's brought everyone pizza for five years. You chipped in three times last month.
Anatoly invites you fishing on Saturday at dawn: “A break from the office.” That means getting up at four.
At the evening team building, everyone has to draw a “portrait of their department.” You drew yours as a coffee machine.
Liza fought with her desk neighbor and sends you a long evening message listing her grievances. He's your friend.
Vlada was late and asks what happened at the stand-up. It lasted forty minutes, and the gist fits in one word.
A lawyer from Legal invites you for coffee “just to chat.” Everyone knows lawyers never just chat.
Ilona shows up at 9:00 a.m. with two coffees: “One's yours if you help with my spreadsheet before lunch.”
All morning the “Gossip” chat has been betting on who'll get promoted. You have the fewest bets. That stings a little.
The company's mailroom asks you to sign for all the team's packages while they're out. They promise “just a couple.”
Your neighbor proposes a morning ritual: ten minutes discussing TV shows “to wake up the brain.” Work is waiting.
Intern Rinat asks if he can use your computer while you're in a meeting. His laptop broke.
Zlata announces she's been put on your task “as backup.” Nobody asked for backup.
right: Go ask the boss about it

text: Someone in the team chat proposed posting a “photo of the day” every morning. You woke up five minutes ago and look like it.
Gena whispers that he forgot his wife's birthday and asks you to cover: “Say I'm in a meeting till midnight.”
Zhora says the head of Marketing is looking for a new hire and “you'd be a great fit.” Interested?
New hire Katya accidentally broke your favorite mug and is crying. It said “Employee of the Month.”
right: Ask her to buy a new one

text: Monday morning, Yefim tells everyone about his weekend: he hiked forty kilometers. You're invited next time.
The office manager wants you to order new chairs for the team. You need to pick from a hundred models by lunch.
right: Hold a vote in the chat

text: Dusya brings in a kitten in a box: “Found it by my building, please take it!” At home, a jealous cat awaits you.
In the “Traffic” chat, coworkers say the whole city is gridlocked. You could say “I'm stuck in traffic” and sleep another half hour.
Your row neighbor stuck a “Smile!” sticky note on your monitor. That's the twentieth one this month.
Philip wants to discuss “a delicate matter” with you over lunch. His face says it'll take a while.
Intern Sonya emailed clients a template that reads “Hello, [NAME]!” Three hundred clients. The boss doesn't know yet.
Taras is taking a two-hour lunch and asks you to answer his calls. His phone rings every five minutes.
Sales is celebrating a closed deal and invited you for cake. The deal closed thanks to your work, but nobody mentioned you.
Ada says you have a “secret admirer” on the team: someone keeps leaving chocolate on your desk.
The team chat wants you to pick the cake for the boss's birthday: honey cake or Napoleon. Everyone else has argued for an hour.
Sitting next to you in the meeting, Yermolay is trying to pin the missed deadline on you. The boss is looking at you.
Rozalia asks you to settle her dispute with Nika: whose turn it is to order water. Both are looking at you like a judge.
The IT guy offers to set up your new computer right now, but you'll have to sit in the kitchen without work for an hour.
Mark spotted a mistake in your presentation five minutes before showtime and announces it in front of everyone.
right: Ask him to tell you privately

text: Inga invites you to a lunchtime dumpling-making class in the cafeteria. You can take the dumplings home after.
Your neighbor has been on the phone with his bank for half an hour, repeating his card number aloud. The whole team knows it by heart.
New guy Borya asks you to explain how things “unofficially” work here. Who's friends with whom, who to fear.
Rostislav suggests writing the boss a joint letter about overtime. Sign it, and you'll be the “ringleader.”
Accounting urgently wants your receipts from a business trip. The trip was six months ago; the receipts are in your jacket.
Natasha is offended you didn't invite her to lunch. You just went to the pharmacy. She's sitting with her back pointedly turned.
Before leaving, Oleg asks if you're free Saturday: he needs to move a wardrobe. “Pizza and soda are on me.”
The office parents' chat needs help with a kids' party on Saturday. They need an entertainer. Everyone's looking at you.
Kirill texts in the evening: “Hey, can I take over your project tomorrow? I need to prove myself.” The project is almost done.
Your neighbor has gone home, but his computer keeps playing an alarm. You don't know his password. It keeps ringing.
The company retreat at a country house. You've been roomed with the company's loudest snorer. It's going to be a long night.
Inessa wants you to be her “productivity partner”: a call every night at nine to discuss plans.
Luka suggests staying late to finish the presentation together. “Faster together,” and then pizza on him.
A coworker from another department invites you to dinner “as friends.” But the chat is already joking you're a couple.
7:00 p.m. Team building: everyone's learning to bake bread. Your loaf didn't rise, and your neighbor's is perfect. The instructor is watching.
Julia texts at 9 p.m. suggesting breakfast together before work tomorrow. Breakfast at 7:30 a.m. at the café by the office.
The chat is deciding who'll help Sales at a trade show on Saturday. You get a day off in return. You dream of your weekend.
Your row neighbor says he overheard management talking about your department. He'll tell you, but “not here, at the bar.”
Nata is going on maternity leave and throwing a farewell party. Everyone's giving touching speeches. It's your turn, and you prepared nothing.
Vanya asks if you want to quit and start a business with him. He's already designed a logo.
Intern Glasha stayed until eight trying to finish your task, which nobody assigned her. She wanted to help.
Timur set up a plant-watering rotation and put you on Friday evening. You leave at five.
10:30 p.m. The team chat erupted into a debate: which soup is better, borscht or solyanka. Two hundred messages, and you've been tagged.
8:50 a.m. Your laptop won't boot: it wants a BIOS update and says don't touch the power for 40 minutes. Stand-up is at 9:00. Just sit and watch the progress bar?
left: Watch the bar with some tea

text: At 9:10 the IT guy announces a mandatory password reset for everyone. A minute later half the department is at his door asking, "What was the old one?" Get in line?
For the third time on the call, the client says, "We can't hear you." You can hear yourself just fine. Maybe the client just doesn't like what you're saying.
You sent an email to "All Staff" that said, "Who even came up with this?" It turns out the CFO came up with it. He's on the list too.
right: Pretend it was about the weather

text: The printer on your floor has learned to talk. In a robot voice it announces: "Paper jam in tray three." It doesn't have a tray three. Go looking?
6:10 p.m. The team's cloud folder is syncing to your laptop and promises to finish in "about 9 hours." You can't close the lid. Wait it out?
The AI cut your 20-page report down to three lines. They sound smart, but there isn't a single number in them. Send it to the boss as a "summary"?
Someone in the team chat asks, "Guys, anyone have a phone charger with that weird plug?" You do, but it's your last one and it lives in your drawer.
left: Lend it, ask for it back

text: The task tracker sent 38 notifications that someone changed a label color. One of them might actually be important. Turn notifications off for good?
In the evening, the only office Wi-Fi that works is called "Guest_NOT_FOR_WORK." The work network went home before you did. Connect?
Since this morning the work messenger shows everyone as "offline," including the people sitting right next to you. Message them or just talk out loud?
right: Wait for it to wake up

text: Email: "You've won a company scooter! Confirm your passport and card number." Signed: "Gifts Department." Your company has no such department.
Your new webcam makes you tanned and toned by default. You can turn off the "beautifier," but that requires admin rights.
6:30 p.m. The boss asks you to "real quick show me how to make slides in that AI thing." His "real quick" usually lasts until nine.
left: Show him in 5 min and leave

text: The scanner spits out every document upside down. Your neighbor says it's easier to stand on your head. What about that 30-page contract?
The VPN gave you an address from another country. Your email is now in a foreign language, and the tracker offers you a day off for a local holiday.
For the third time today, a coworker asks how to attach a file to an email. You've shown him twice already. He's looking at you hopefully.
7:00 p.m. You accidentally hit "Reply All" on the gift collection email. Now 300 people know you're "out, broke till payday."
You have 30 seconds to come up with a new password or you're locked out. All you can think of is your cat's name and your birth year. Type it in?
The IT guy walks in and silently unplugs your computer from the network: "Virus." You only opened a spreadsheet with macros from Accounting.
A 12-person call, and someone has renovation going on: a hammer drill that pauses exactly when you speak. Muting them will take forever.
Your phone has been at 3% since morning. The only free outlet is by the boss's desk, and he's already in. Charge at his desk?
In the evening you asked the AI to write a birthday note to your mother-in-law. It suggested "taking her engagement to the next level." Send it?
Someone filed a "Fix the task tracker" ticket in the task tracker. The tracker is down, so the ticket won't open. Who's going to do it?
The printer only prints in "toner saver" mode: the text is as pale as you look on Monday. Take the contract to the client like this?
In the evening you set your status to "Do Not Disturb." A minute later a coworker writes: "Sorry to disturb, just saw you're not being disturbed."
You deleted an "extra" folder called "old" from the shared cloud. A minute later the accountant bursts into chat: the annual report was in "old."
Morning call, and your laptop camera shows only your forehead. Propping it up on books means dismantling your stack of reports.
Security is running a drill: a "phishing" link for free pizza landed in chat. You already clicked it. No pizza arrived, but a reprimand did.
At home, the Wi-Fi only works in the bathroom. On the evening call you're perched on the edge of the tub, and the echo makes you sound very convincing.
The IT guy is handing out new mice. You get a pink one with LEDs that goes "pew" on every click. There are no others.
The boss sent you "his thoughts" for a presentation. Judging by "it's important to note" and "in today's world," it's clear where they came from. Say something?
9:00 p.m. Your laptop lid won't close: the hinge cracked. The laptop just sits there open, like it's expecting more work from you.
right: Cover it with a towel, sleep

text: The email system sent a key client's message to spam. The client has been calling the boss for three hours, and the boss is staring right at you.
After an overnight update, every desktop icon became an identical gray square. Your report is somewhere among them. Start hunting?
left: Open the squares one by one
right: Get coffee till it fixes itself

text: On the call, everyone started talking at once and then went silent at once. The silence has lasted nine seconds now. Who speaks first?
The evening team chat is arguing about which messenger is best. 140 messages, all in the work messenger everyone hates. Chime in?
To scan your passport for HR, you need a six-digit code. The HR lady has the code, and she's on the phone with the scanner. Wait?
A coworker asks for the shared account password. You know it by heart, but IT banned saying it out loud. Whisper it?
On your way out, you notice your charger is gone from the outlet. Someone in the next office is still working, and their laptop is your brand.
The company AI greets you every morning and asks about your mood. Today it suggested you "talk about this with your manager."
The boss asks you to print an email so he can read it and then have you scan it back so he can forward it. Suggest just forwarding it?
Before leaving, you drag your cards to "Done." One stubbornly jumps back to "In Progress" — someone keeps dragging it back.
right: Ask in chat who it is

text: The work messenger added reactions. Now every message you send the boss gets just a thumbs-up, even "Can I take vacation?"
The IT guy offers a deal: he sets you up with a second monitor, and you bring him pastries from the cafeteria all month. You really want that monitor.
You ended the call and said loudly, "Finally!" The "Leave" button kicked in a second later than you thought.
The printer mixes your document with someone else's résumé. It's your neighbor's, and it's for a competitor. Return it to him personally?
A "sysadmin from headquarters" calls asking you to read him the code from a text "for verification." The voice is suspiciously cheerful for IT.
Your phone offers to update overnight. You have an early call tomorrow, and the last update wiped your alarm. Risk it?
The cloud folder with the client deck is "access on request." The request went to the owner, and the owner is out sick.
5:58 p.m. The laptop says: "2 minutes of battery remaining." That's exactly how long is left in the workday. Coincidence or a sign?
In the evening an email arrives marked "Not urgent, but by morning." Open it now and ruin your evening. Don't open it and ruin your morning.
At 10:40 p.m. a coworker messages: "You asleep?" Nothing else. The typing dots have been appearing and disappearing for ten minutes.
You ask the AI to plan a week of meals so you don't have to think in the evenings. It suggests "a quick 14-ingredient dinner in just 3 hours."
6:20 p.m. On your way out, the IT guy asks you to "just sit with him" while he reboots the server. He's scared to do it alone. Stay?
Evening call, and someone in your building starts drilling. You're the only one with your mic on, because you're the one presenting.
Your neighbor changed the password on the Wi-Fi you've been secretly using for three years. The evening call starts in ten minutes. Knock on his door?
You get home and realize your laptop charger is still at the office, and tomorrow you're working from home. Go back for it?
7:00 p.m. The tracker sends your weekly summary: "You closed 2 tasks and opened 17." A copy went to the boss automatically.
On your way out you set the auto-reply to "I'm on vacation" instead of "In a meeting." Your vacation is a month away, and it already went to a client.
Your TV, phone, and laptop all demand updates at the same time. You can spend the evening on progress or on your show.
You forgot to close your laptop, and for the whole evening call your camera showed the kitchen ceiling. Everyone assumed it was intentional.
A coworker asks the AI to "prep you for tomorrow's talk with the boss." The AI generates 40 questions, every one of them a trap.
An evening text: "Your work account is locked, follow this link." The link goes to a site with three typos in the address.
right: Delete it and go to bed

text: At 9:00 p.m. someone posted a meme about the boss in the team chat. The boss is in the chat. It was deleted within a minute, but you'd already reacted "haha."
6:30 p.m. The printer is finally fixed and is happily printing everything queued up all week. 600 pages. Half of them are your drafts.
At home you open the cloud folder and see a coworker has been editing your document all evening. A cursor with his name is darting through your text.
Mom asks you over video chat to "take a look at what's wrong with my phone." The camera is pointed at the chandelier, and only you have sound. Help?
left: Fix it over video all night

text: 7:15 p.m. The boss sent you a 6-minute voice message. The messenger's transcript reads: "So, basically, there's this thing, you know." Listen now?
To check work email tonight, you need the VPN. The VPN needs a code from an app, the app needs an update, and the update needs Wi-Fi.
In the evening you accidentally sent a pizza photo meant for a friend to the work chat. Your coworkers are already discussing the toppings.
Your laptop died while saving the report. When you turn it back on, the file contains only the heading "Report" and your last name.
The host wraps up the evening webinar: "Any questions?" Only your "Raise hand" button is lit — you clicked it by accident.
8:30 a.m. 140 emails in your inbox, and exactly one titled "Re: Re: Re: Fwd: Important." Scroll through the whole 60-reply thread?
right: Reply "What do you need from me?"

text: The office Wi-Fi only works by the window with the ficus. A coworker with a laptop and a thermos has already claimed the ficus spot. Squeeze in?
right: Plug in a cable in the corner

The boss demands that morning emails include an "AI summary." The summary of your summary is longer than the summary itself.

The new printer requires a badge to log in. It doesn't recognize yours and prints everyone else's names on your pages. Print the report "as someone else"?
A coworker asks to borrow your headset "for five minutes" for a call. Last time he returned it a week later, missing an ear cushion.
right: Say you have a call yourself

text: In the morning you discover your laptop didn't charge overnight: someone switched off the power strip to save energy. Battery's at 9%. Where to charge?
This morning the tracker has a new column, "Discussing," and all your tasks moved there by themselves. The discussion is scheduled for "someday."
At 9:05 the messenger set your status to "Away," though you're sitting there typing. The boss writes: "Where are you so early in the day?"
left: Send a selfie at your desk

9:00 a.m. You open your laptop and see someone else's desktop: bags got mixed up at reception. You have the accountant's laptop.
right: Wait for him to show up

text: Morning call with a client, and captions are on by accident. Your "good morning" got transcribed as "good mourning." The client looks concerned.
This morning email offers a "Send later" feature. You can write to the boss now and schedule it for 8:00 a.m., as if you'd been at work for ages.
IT introduced one-time login codes. The code goes to your phone, and your phone is at home on the nightstand. Go back?
A coworker admits the AI writes all his emails and offers you "a really good prompt." The boss praises his emails every day.
Since this morning your wireless mouse moves the cursor on its own. It seems it paired with your neighbor, who's scrolling the news.
Lunch call, "no agenda, just to chat." Everyone's chewing on camera, and someone's already talking about their cacti. Stay?
The IT guy asks who in your department is "the one who clicks on everything." Everyone looks at the intern. The intern looks at you.
The boss asks you to send an email "on his behalf." You're about to hit "Send" when you notice the signature: "Best regards, your kitty."
right: Ask the boss if it's for real

text: Someone attached a GIF of a burning house to your card on the task board. Your deadline is tomorrow and it's not on fire. Yet.
You search the cloud for "Final." You get 48 files: "Final," "Final_new," "Final_really_final," and "Final (2) copy." Which one to open?
The AI promised to transcribe the meeting minutes. In the end, every decision in the minutes was made by "Participant Inaudible."
After lunch the printer starts printing on its own. Thirty pages of someone's vacation photos. The last one shows your boss in a sun hat.
left: Give the photos to the boss
right: Pin the sun hat on the board

text: You recorded a voice message for a coworker, forgetting that a bonus discussion was going on right next to you. It's already sent. You couldn't preview it.
Email from "the CEO": "Urgently buy $500 in gift cards, tell no one." The CEO's address is on a free email domain.
The cafeteria Wi-Fi only works at the serving counter. You're waiting for an important email and have gotten in line for meatballs twice now just to check it.
On the call, the client asks you to "share your screen." You have 34 tabs open, including "how to politely say no to a client." Which window do you show?
The IT guy is giving a cybersecurity lecture. He types the projector password in front of everyone: "Admin123." The room silently writes it down.
The AI generated a logo for the new project. The boss loves it, but you notice the word "PROJECT" is spelled with a mystery letter. Say something?
You get an email cc'ing someone listed as "Vasya (do not add)." He was added. Vasya is already replying all: "Why am I 'do not add'?"
You're three minutes late to the call. To get in, you have to wait for the organizer to "admit you from the lobby." The organizer is in the bathroom.
The color printer turns everything shades of green. Your sales chart looks like a lawn. The presentation for management is in an hour.
right: Redo it in black and white

text: A coworker asks you to send him a file. It's 2 GB, email allows 20 MB, and you don't trust the cloud. There's a USB stick in your drawer.
The manager wants time logged in the tracker in 15-minute chunks. Logging your time takes you 15 minutes every hour.
You've been added to the "Friday Lunch" chat. It's Wednesday, and there are already 300 messages about picking a restaurant. You don't want to go anywhere.
The company's cloud storage is full. IT asks everyone to free up 5 GB. Your 5 GB are videos from the office party.
right: Move them to a USB stick

text: Your laptop runs so hot you could warm up lunch on it. Your neighbor has already put his sandwich on the lid. The fan is sobbing.
A coworker forwards a "fun quiz: which fruit are you?" To see your result, you have to enter your work email and password. He's already a banana.
The scanner saves files with names like "doc_000017384.pdf." You need to find Tuesday's scan among 400 others just like it.
In the meeting the boss asks, "Did you write this, or the AI?" You wrote it, but the phrasing came out so smooth nobody believes you.
The meeting room Wi-Fi drops every time someone uses the microwave next door. It's lunchtime, and you have a presentation.
On the call you're asked to "raise your hand" for questions. Looking for the button, you accidentally send everyone applause. For the fifth time.
The IT guy says your problem will be solved by "a simple restart." You've restarted 7 times. He suggests an eighth.
You forgot to attach the file to a client email. You resent it and forgot again. A third email would be fatal to your reputation.
Asked "How many vacation days do I have?", the company HR chatbot replies: "Vacation is an important part of life." No numbers.
On an after-lunch call you realize there's spinach in your teeth and the camera is in HD. Someone just asked you to smile.
You've been assigned a task called "Look into it." No description, no deadline, no project. Created by: System. Who's behind the system is unknown.
The office set up a "phone charging station" at reception. Your phone is there at 70%, but you're waiting for a client's call.
You replied "ok" instead of "Ok." in the work messenger, and for two hours a coworker has been asking if you're all right.
Marketing replaced the intern with an AI. Now the AI asks you to "explain the task in more detail" every ten minutes.
You connected to the VPN and learned all your internet now goes through the office. Including your lunchtime show. IT sees everything.
You wake up to a notification: "Petrova added you to 'Gift for the Boss.'" At 6:45 a.m. The collection has begun, $20 minimum.
This morning your laptop's spacebar is dead. Every email looks like a long magic spell: "Goodmorning,attachingthereport."
The printer is finally fixed, with a note on it: "Don't touch anything except the Print button." There is no Print button.
Morning call, and your kid asks off-screen: "Is that the man you call 'him again'?" Your mic is on.
IT banned personal USB drives this morning. You brought the work deck on a kitty-themed USB stick. The scanner at the entrance beeps.
Only the chief accountant knows the accounting software password, and she's on vacation at the beach. Call her about "something urgent"?
Morning stand-up over the tracker: everyone says their task is "in progress." You look at yours — it's been in progress for 4 months.
9:20 a.m. Your inbox has an invite: "Sync on the Sync." Agenda: sync up on the results of the last sync.
This morning you can't open your work document: "File moved to trash by owner." The owner is you. When did that happen?
The new official call background is the company logo on a sunset beach. Everyone must use it. Your camera doesn't support it.
Morning. Your AI assistant sorted your email on its own and filed the boss's message under "Newsletters." The boss has been waiting since 8:00.
Every morning the office Wi-Fi makes you accept a 40-point user agreement. Today there's a new point: "I agree to arrive on time."
You have the last cable on the floor that charges the new phones. Since morning, a little line of coworkers has formed at your desk.
This morning the messenger requires a "mandatory identity check": a selfie with your left eyebrow raised. Your eyebrow won't go up.
right: Use the messenger on your phone

text: Security introduces a "clean desk" policy: clear everything when you go to lunch. Your desk is home to a cactus, three mugs, and a year's archive.
In the evening you remember you emailed a client starting with "Dear Anatoly." The client's name is Anastasia.
At home you ask the AI to explain fractions to your kid. It does it so well your kid asks why you can't explain things like that.
right: Hand the kid over to the AI

text: 6:40 p.m. The IT guy calls: someone is trying to log in with your account from another city. You're home and haven't gone anywhere.
right: Ask him to do it for you

text: At home that evening your laptop keeps suggesting you "turn on rest mode." It doesn't know you have a deadline in the morning.
Evening family video call with relatives. Your aunt has spent half an hour learning to unmute. You can't hear her, but you can see she's outraged.
right: Wait for her to give up

text: 7:30 p.m. The team chat is discussing tomorrow's "quick" task. If you stay quiet, it goes to you. If you reply, it also goes to you.
Friday evening. The tracker sends a reminder: "Don't forget to fill out your weekly report." The report has 22 required fields.
As you head home, your phone auto-connects to the office Wi-Fi and starts a 3 GB update download. IT won't be happy.
Right before bed you see an email from the boss: "Let's discuss tomorrow." That's it. The subject line is empty. It's going to be a long night.
In the evening the messenger shows your message to the boss was "read" three hours ago. No reply. Just silence and two blue checkmarks.
right: Go for a walk, no phone

text: 8:40 a.m. IT installs a "productivity app" on everyone's machine that takes a screenshot every five minutes. Your first screenshot: solitaire.
left: Close it and get to work

text: The morning call opens with a poll: "How did you sleep?" with answer options. "Badly, because of this call" isn't one of them.
Your new laptop has a sticker from the previous owner: "If you're reading this — run." The IT guy says it's a joke.
At 7:50 a.m. an all-staff email arrives with a 200 MB attachment. Your mailbox is blocked until noon for being "over quota."
The boss started a morning ritual: everyone asks the AI "How can I be more productive?" and reads the answer at stand-up. The answers are identical.
The printer broke, and the office manager hung a sign on it: "I'm tired." Coworkers have left tea and cookies next to it. Add yours?
This morning every task in the tracker got an "assignee happiness index." Yours is 2 out of 10. The boss already sent: "Let's talk."
The office router decided your laptop is a "suspicious device" and only lets you online for 10 minutes an hour.
Your charging cable is stretched across the aisle because the outlet is far away. Three people have tripped on it this morning. Move your desk?
9:05 a.m. You've been mentioned in 14 threads this morning. Even an "@everyone" from a chat you were added to by mistake got you.
This morning the team agreed to turn cameras on "for team spirit." You woke up five minutes ago, and it really shows.
The entrance now has facial recognition. After the weekend it doesn't recognize you and calls you "Unknown Guest Number Seven."
This morning the cloud says you're over your limit and blocks uploads. Your limit is 1 GB. Your presentation is 1.2 GB.
right: Send a link to a USB stick

text: A coworker asks how to make the AI "answer like me." You can tell he wants to train it to go to stand-ups in his place.
Back from vacation, you type your password, and your fingers type your home Wi-Fi password. Three tries, locked out, IT will come after lunch.
This morning you discovered that yesterday you hit "Reply All" with "Thank you!" It spawned 40 replies of "You're welcome!"
This morning the scanner wants to "calibrate the image" and asks you to scan a blank sheet. No blank paper: the printer only has forms.
The client shares his screen on the call, and a notification pops up in the corner: "Don't forget to tell them the budget got cut." Everyone sees it.
The AI made you a "perfect" spreadsheet. An hour later it turns out it made up half the numbers "so it would look nice."
The IT guy is quitting and handing out his "inheritance": keyboards to some, cables to others. You get responsibility for the printer.
Your draft reply to a client — "Oh, come on, what now?!" — accidentally got sent. The client replies: "Agreed! What now?!" The thread has livened up.
The messenger is launching "Emoji of the Week." Voting happens in the 400-person general chat, and every vote is a separate message.
Your neighbor accidentally connected your laptop to his monitor. Now your laptop thinks it's his monitor and shows his screen.
After lunch a task from the boss appears in the tracker: "Do what I said this morning." You didn't see him this morning.
A coworker asks you to hold the server room door while he "runs out for a sec" to grab a cable. He has no badge. He looks confident.
Office Wi-Fi is now paid for "non-corporate devices." The work phone you were issued a year ago is suddenly "non-corporate."
You joined the call and accidentally picked the "Office" background. While sitting in the actual office. Coworkers joke you work in two places at once.
You were given access to the "Management Only" cloud folder instead of "Reports." The folder looks interesting. Report the mistake?
The printer adds your name to the bottom of every page because you once set up a "signature." Today every contract in the department went out like that.
The chatbot at the company's bank has been telling you "Your question is very important to us" for four hours. The question: when will the payment arrive?
The boss decided AI can replace meetings. Now everyone writes their thoughts to it, and it replies: "Let's discuss this in a meeting."
6:15 p.m. Your laptop suddenly maxes the volume and blasts your "Songs for Tears and Reports" playlist through the office. The boss is still here.
On his way out, the IT guy asks you not to turn anything off tonight, "or it'll break." At home your kettle's boiling and your cat's waiting. The office hums.
right: At least turn off the monitor

text: In the evening you notice your mailbox has a rule: "Forward everything to personal email." Nobody knows who set it up. 300 emails are already at home.
Evening call with foreign partners. The AI interpreter renders your joke so that everyone nods seriously and takes notes.
You ask the AI how to leave early without hurting things with the boss. It replies: "Discuss this with your manager."
You're already on the subway, and the work messenger on your phone buzzes every 30 seconds. Looks like the chat is on fire. Or it's lunch talk again.
At home you realize you swapped phone and laptop chargers with your desk neighbor. You have his, he has yours, and he lives across town.
right: Buy a new one on the way

text: In the evening you try to finish the report at a café. You only get the Wi-Fi password if you buy dessert. Dessert costs $9.
8:00 p.m. The tracker sends a survey: "Rate your workload from 1 to 10." Answer honestly — the boss will see the results.
In the evening you save personal photos to the cloud and realize it's the work cloud. And the folder is shared with the whole department.
7:00 p.m. You're secretly printing concert tickets on the work printer. The boss walks out of his office straight to the printer for his papers.
Before bed an email arrives: "Confirm your attendance at the office party." The link leads to a form asking for a "card number to reserve."
On the evening call you zoned out and started singing along to music in your headphones. Mic on. The song: your old summer camp anthem.
In the evening the IT guy calls you at home: "Do you happen to know where our server room is?" He sounds unsure, with an alarm going off behind him.
8:30 p.m. You open your email "just to peek," and there's the client's answer to a question you've waited a week on. The answer: "No."
In the evening you discover your laptop hasn't updated in six months. Updates will take 3 hours, and without them you can't log in tomorrow.
left: Start it and go to bed

text: Mom texts in the evening: "Is it true your boss is a robot? I saw on the news that AI is replacing everyone."
You can't sleep, so you ask the AI for an excuse for tomorrow's stand-up. It suggests "an insight leak."
As you close your laptop for the night, you notice the camera is covered with gum. Who did it — your neighbor, IT, or stressed-out you?
The new "smart" coffee machine is on Wi-Fi and wants you to log in to an account. Only the IT guy knows the password, and he drinks tea.
This morning IT sends out a "Spot the Phish" quiz. The very first email in it looks exactly like a real one from your boss.
8:55 a.m. The link to the morning call wants you to install a new app. Installing takes 12 minutes; the call starts in five.
In the morning the boss asks everyone to stop using "Reply All" and reply only to him. A minute later he replies all: "Everyone clear?"
This morning your laptop asks for a password you definitely never set. The hint: "You know." You don't.
Your AI assistant signed you up for a "team morning run" at 7:30 a.m. Its own initiative. The team is already waiting.
The morning printer line is eight people long. Someone's printing a book, someone photos, and you need one page for the boss to sign.
The messenger offers "dark mode" and switches it on immediately. Now the boss complains your spreadsheets look "gloomy" in screenshots.
This morning you have 0 tasks in the tracker. For the first time in a year. Something's wrong: either you've been fired or the tracker broke.
The wireless charger on your desk only works at one precise angle. You found it. The phone now lies there like a monument; it must not be touched.
This morning you try to connect to "Office_5G," and it says, "Device not supported." Your neighbor with a 2009 laptop is already online.
A coworker puts a "Runs on Coffee" sticker on his laptop. A week later everyone has one, and you're the only tea drinker. Fit in?
This morning you realized your camera mirrors the text on your T-shirt. For the past month, your "COFFEE" shirt has read "EEFFOC."
The team's cloud folder was renamed "Archive_do_not_touch." All current work is in it. Work in the archive or organize a move?
Security is introducing two-factor authentication even for the coffee machine. The code takes two minutes to arrive. You need coffee now.
IT turned on a "smart VPN" that decides on its own which sites are work-related. In its opinion, your work email is not.
The scanner on your floor only works with the hallway door open. There's a draft, papers fly away, and you need to scan 20 pages.
You forgot to turn off "noise cancellation" on the call. Now you can only be heard when you shout. Everyone's a little scared.
The IT guy asks you into the server room to "help hold something." It's a cable you can't let go of for about forty minutes. It's nice and cool in there.
left: Go hold it in the cool

text: A coworker sent a client an AI-written email without reading it. The client asks you what "your quantum business synthesis" means.
At lunch you decided to clean up your email and accidentally deleted the entire Inbox. The trash empties every 30 minutes.
The tracker introduced "story points." The team has spent an hour arguing how many points "Order water" is worth. Third round of voting.
You messaged a coworker that the new boss is "not bad, I guess." The conversation turned out to be a group chat, and the new boss is in it.
After lunch the printer demands to be "fed" 11x17 paper. The office only has letter size. A sign says: "No 11x17, no work."
Your cloud spreadsheet is open for 25 people at once. Multicolored cursors are darting around. Someone just deleted your column.
After lunch the whole team sits in one corner, because that's the only place with Wi-Fi. Your desk is by the door. Move closer?
You get an email from "the bank": "Confirm your payroll card." You were just expecting an advance on your paycheck yesterday. The link looks almost real.
Your laptop's Delete key fell off. You found it an hour later — in a cup of tea. The cup, by the way, was yours.
On an after-lunch call you're asked to "turn on your camera so we can see emotions." After the cafeteria, you only have one emotion: sleepy.
Your laptop charging cord is wrapped in blue electrical tape. Coworkers joke it's older than the intern. IT promises a replacement in a month.
Evening office party over video. The host proposes a "funniest background" contest. You're in curlers with no background.
In the evening email suggests a "smart reply" to the boss: "Yes, of course, I'll do it today!" Today is already over. Click it?
In the evening your AI assistant offers to "sum up the day." Its summary: "You did great work." You know you didn't.
7:20 p.m. The IT guy asks everyone to turn off their computers "for a sec" to test the network. Yours takes 25 minutes to shut down.
In the evening the laptop offers to "install a search assistant." You click "No" for the fifth time. The sixth time, it doesn't ask.
In the evening you find a message from yourself to yourself: "Don't forget!!!" What not to forget is unknown.
In the evening you're tagged in 9 tasks with "take a look when you have a minute." You won't have a minute until 2030.
At home the Wi-Fi drops every time your neighbor turns on his kettle. Your evening call lasts exactly until his tea time.
An evening notification: "340 files added to your cloud folder." The intern added them. The folder is named "Don't Look."
6:40 p.m. The last printer that works after six says "Getting ready." It's been getting ready for 20 minutes.
In the evening you see your "See you Monday!" auto-reply has been on since last Wednesday. Clients have been getting it on every email for a week.
In the evening security asks you to complete "After-6 p.m. Safety" training. It's a 40-minute video, and the turnstile won't let you out without it.
9:00 p.m. A former coworker invites you to a "friendly video call" but actually wants you to get him rehired. It's hard to say no on video.
In the evening you finally find an AI that writes reports for you. It costs a week's salary. Subscribe?
7:00 p.m. As you leave, a coworker asks to borrow your charger "overnight." Tomorrow you're working from home with your laptop. Lend it?
left: Lend it, work at the office

text: In the evening the IT guy posts "Top 5 Weirdest Passwords in the Department" in the group chat. Yours is #3. No name, but everyone guessed.
You're taking the laptop home, and on the subway it starts blasting the video call ringtone at full volume. The whole car is staring at you.
Late in the evening the intern writes in the team chat: "Does anyone know how to delete a message sent to the wrong person?"
right: Go to bed, stay out of it

text: In the evening a stranger writes: "Your boss asked you to urgently wire money to this account." The boss is on vacation. Or is he?
The new ergonomic keyboard is split into two halves. After lunch you're still typing "Hlelo," and your neighbor laughs at every email.
left: Go back to the old one

text: 9:05 a.m. HR calls: your employment contract lists your title as “Rocket Sales Manager.” Re-sign it now?
right: Keep the rockets as a souvenir

text: Safety induction: “Sign here to confirm you attended.” The induction hasn’t started yet. Sign in advance?
10:20 a.m. Sirens: evacuation drill. You have a 40-page unsaved report open. Leave right away?
Accounting wants the original receipt from a business trip three months ago. It’s faded to a blank slip of paper. Bring it anyway?
8:30 a.m., company checkup. Fasting blood test — and someone just brought fresh croissants into the office. Hold out?
The learning portal has a mandatory course, “Email Etiquette”: 120 slides, due at noon today. Skim it?
HR wants your annual goals: five of them, each “measurable, ambitious and realistic.” Be honest?
The timesheet marks you absent last Tuesday. You ran the team meeting that day, in front of everyone. Go sort it out?
Legal wants the contract approved by 11:00 with comments in “track changes.” The contract arrived as a scan. Now what?
The team chat is voting on when to run the engagement survey: “morning,” “evening” or “instead of lunch.” Vote?
The office manager needs someone to sign the safety log for the whole team: “You don’t mind, right? Your handwriting is lovely.” Sign?
8:50 a.m. Your payslip arrives: 14 lines of earnings, 15 of deductions. The total is $30 less than usual. Look into it?
Boss: “Sign the vacation rescheduling order, it’s just a formality.” It moves your vacation to November. Sign?
The portal wants a badge photo “on a light background, no expression.” The nearest light background is the restroom door. Shoot there?
Civil defense drill: put on a gas mask and reach the basement in 30 seconds. You’re wearing a brand-new shirt. Join in?
HR needs a copy of your diploma. The original is at your mom’s in another city, and the copy is probably at your ex’s. What now?
Accounting reminds you: expense reports are due within three days. Your trip ended yesterday. File it today?
right: Do it on the last day

text: A coworker asks you to sign his income statement “as a witness.” It looks slightly homemade. Sign it?
9:00 a.m. The “Effective Communication” training opens with the trainer failing to switch on the mic for half an hour. Help out?
Legal sends a new policy: every client email must be reviewed by them first. Your client has been waiting an hour. Send anyway?
HR wants a personal data form: “Relatives up to second cousins, and where they work.” You have no idea where your uncle works.
The boss forwards the vacation schedule: “Check who’s covering for whom.” You’re covering for three people in the same week.
right: Accept it and make a plan

text: HR: “Today is mentoring day — everyone shares one life hack with a newbie.” Your only life hack is where to hide from HR.
8:45 a.m. The chief accountant calls: “I need your signature right now, the courier’s waiting downstairs.” You’re still on the subway.
Fire inspection: under your desk is a power strip plugged into another power strip. The inspector frowns.
HR asks you to review your new job description. It lists 48 duties, including “maintaining a positive atmosphere.”
The drivers’ morning checkup now applies to everyone: breathalyzer and blood pressure. Yours is 150.
A coworker wants to swap vacation weeks: he gets July, you get November. In return he promises “eternal gratitude.”
New accounting rule: all receipts must be glued to letter paper “in neat rows, no overlapping.” You have 37 taxi receipts.
A courier brings documents to sign: 60 pages, a signature on each, plus initials in the margins. Sign now?
The boss wants a quarterly KPI report, but the template is last year’s and half the metrics no longer exist. What do you write?
HR invites you to “Breakfast with the Director”: five random employees and one omelet. You’re on the list. Go?
The safety officer is inspecting chairs: yours “fails ergonomic standards” and is replaced with a stool until a new one arrives.
right: Hide your chair at a neighbor’s

text: The timekeeper logs you in at 9:01. “One minute late — write an explanation.” Do it?
right: Show the time on your phone

text: Accounting sent your salary to an old card you closed six months ago. The money is somewhere between worlds. What now?
right: Wait for it to come back

text: Legal wants “all project documents for the past three years” by noon. Half of them are messenger chats.
Boss: “You took that Excel course, right? Teach the team at 11.” You took it in your sleep. Literally.
HR wants you to sign a personal data consent form — the fifth this year. Each has a clause about “photos without consent.”
HR introduces a daily “mood check-in”: pick an emoji by 10:00. Everyone picks the sun. You feel like a rain cloud.
Someone from the next department whispers: “Word is, bonuses only go to people who finish the security course by lunch.” Believe it?
The chief accountant wants your memo redone: not “please pay for my taxi” but “I hereby petition for reimbursement of transportation expenses.”
The boss has put you on the peer review committee. The first session is today — and they’re reviewing your friend.
Accounting calls: “Your expense report has a $300 lunch. For one person?” It was lunch with a client and his three kids.
1:00 p.m. HR hosts a “lunch webinar” on burnout. You watch it instead of having lunch. Join?
Legal spotted “we guarantee results” in your email to a client and demands a retraction. The client is already celebrating.
HR tells you you’ve piled up 46 unused vacation days. “If they expire, don’t blame us.” Take a whole month?
The team chat is debating whether a runny nose justifies a sick day: “heroism” vs. “inhumane.” You sneeze.
right: Wear a mask at your desk

text: Working-at-heights safety training: mandatory for anyone who “might stand on a chair.” It runs until 4 p.m. Go?
right: Promise never to stand on a chair

text: Accounting wants you to reconcile statements with a contractor: 200 lines, 17 cents off. Hunt it down?
Boss: “This quarter’s bonus goes to the best cost-saving idea.” Your idea: fewer meetings.
2:10 p.m. HR noticed your last name is spelled one way in your records and another on your passport. You need an archive certificate. Go?
At sales training you have to “sell” a pen to a colleague. The colleague is your boss, and he’s fully in character.
HR sends a survey: “Rate your manager anonymously.” At the bottom there’s a field “Full name (optional)” — and it’s highlighted.
Accounting wants an explanation: “Pizza, 8 pies, meeting.” The meeting minutes list three people. What do you say?
Legal wants 4 pages of fine-print disclaimers added to the client deck. The deck is 3 slides long.
A coworker came back from sick leave “just to finish a report” and is coughing over the whole row. Ask him to leave?
Fire drill: everyone’s out in the yard being counted. They’ve lost count three times, and you’re standing in the wind without a jacket.
right: Slip into the café across the street

text: The boss asks you to set your KPIs for next quarter “with a stretch.” You put 100%; he changes it to 140%. Argue?
Accounting takes lunch from 1 to 2, and you need the chief accountant’s signature by 2 for a payment. The door is shut; spoons are clinking behind it.
Your external course is approved, with a catch: leave within two years and you repay the full cost. Sign the training agreement?
HR puts up an “Employee of the Month” board in the lobby. They used your badge photo. Ask them to swap it?
HR recalculated your tenure: you’ve worked one day less than you thought, and you’re one day short for your vacation.
The KPI committee wants to know why your customer satisfaction is 99%, not 100%. One client answered “meh.”
Company chat poll: “Who’s coming to the Saturday stress-resilience training?” So far only you — by accident.
Accounting says your bonus has been approved but will be paid “after the quarter closes.” The quarter never closes. Ask for a date?
Legal says don’t sign the supplier contract; the boss says sign it now. They’re both looking at you.
You’re called in to sign a coworker’s disciplinary notice “as an informed witness.” You didn’t see anything.
The first aid room offers a flu shot “right now, while there’s vaccine left.” You’ll feel sluggish until evening.
Records sends your memo back: wrong font, wrong margins, and “Dear” must be “Dear Colleague.” Redo it?
HR offers a “What’s your team personality type?” test. Your manager will see the results. Answer truthfully?
Accounting needs receipts for the party you organized. The host gave you a bill written on a napkin.
The boss wants the vacation schedule to “show the team isn’t empty all summer.” Everyone wants July. Move people around?
A coworker came back from leadership training and now runs a “soul stand-up” every morning. You’re on his team.
The safety officer runs an unscheduled briefing: there’s now a “risk of falling staplers” in the office. Minutes are being taken.
Notification: “You have failed the policy knowledge check.” You’ve never heard of this policy.
HR says a vacation abroad needs a letter from your employer. Three people sign it, and two are on vacation.
Accounting says claiming an education tax credit needs a letter from your university. It changed its name years ago.
The boss calls you in for your annual review. Your score is already penciled in on the form: “3 out of 5.”
HR invites you to be an employer brand ambassador: smile in photos for job ads. Payment: a certificate.
Legal: “Delete the office party photo from social media now — there’s an NDA visible in it.” It’s your best photo ever.
right: Blur the NDA and keep it

text: Accounting rejects your receipt: “This is a restaurant, but your trip was listed as a sports event.” It was a steakhouse called The Athlete.
Training wants you to take a post-training test: 30 questions, 90% to pass. You dozed through half the training.
A coworker whispers: “Accounting mixed it up — I got your bonus.” He offers to “pay you back in cash, someday.”
The floor fire warden was fired. The new warden is you — appointed by electronic order.
Someone shared a vacation request template in the team chat with the date set to 2019 by mistake. Everyone has already used it.
At emotional intelligence training you’re asked to name your emotion “in the moment.” Your emotion is hunger.
HR asks you to pick a slot for your mandatory chest X-ray: “Tuesday at 7:00 a.m. or Friday at 6:30 p.m.” Which one?
Accounting switched to new software: all past expense reports were “lost in migration.” You need to resubmit them.
Boss: “Starting Monday, daily progress reports at 4:45 p.m.” The report has to include how long you spent writing the report.
Legal asks you to rewrite a client email without the words “definitely,” “guarantee” or “certainly.” The email was about lunch.
Security won’t let you onto the accounting floor: “Only with a pass request.” The request is issued by accounting — where you’re headed.
HR needs a volunteer for the union meeting. Perk: a day off. Catch: next year you’re the chair.
HR runs a “stay interview”: “What could make you leave?” The honest answer: interviews like this.
A coworker wants a sick day but fears the boss. He asks you to “lay the groundwork” by mentioning he was coughing.
The chief accountant gathers everyone responsible for assets for a “reconciliation hour.” You’re responsible for a coffee machine that isn’t on the books.
Contest announced: “In-House Trainer of the Year.” The winner teaches newbies on Friday evenings.
Boss at 3 p.m.: “I need a team workload report by 4. In percent, so it’s clear we’re overloaded.”
Legal won’t sign off on the contract without your “memo justifying its expediency.” It’s obvious to everyone except Legal.
HR needs copies of the team’s employment contracts. The copier says “replace toner,” and the toner is with Procurement.
Accounting sent a satisfaction survey about accounting. It’s anonymous — but you log in with your work account.
5:50 p.m. The accountant catches you at the elevator: “We close the month tomorrow — I need your expense report today.” The receipts are at home in your other jacket.
left: Go get them and come back

text: 6:10 p.m. HR sends an order: starting tomorrow you’re “acting head” while your boss is on vacation. No extra pay.
The boss on his way out: “I’ll sign your vacation request once you find cover for the full two weeks.” Everyone’s already gone home.
Mom calls: “Are you on sick leave? You sound hoarse.” You’ve spent all day answering calls from accounting.
7:30 p.m. The team chat gets an engagement survey link: “4 hours left.” The survey has 60 questions.
left: Fill it out on your phone
right: Leave it till the last minute

text: 6:40 p.m. Legal writes: “We didn’t send that contract to the client, did we?” You sent it at lunch — at his own request.
Mandatory evening webinar: “Information Security.” The host says never to open suspicious links — then sends a link to the quiz.
6:20 p.m. The accountant in chat: “You were overpaid on your advance — return it by end of day.” It’s already been spent on groceries.
A coworker invites you after work to discuss “how to get our bonuses.” The plan: the whole team files a complaint. Are you in?
HR invites you to an evening “values round table.” There will be pastries and values worksheets.
6:50 p.m. The boss wants your “annual self-assessment” by morning, “free-form, but in the template.”
On your way out you remember you never applied for the hardship allowance — the deadline is 6:00. It’s 5:58.
HR calls at 7 p.m.: “You skipped your medical checkup — you’ll be suspended Monday.” You did it yesterday and have the paperwork.
6:40 p.m. The fire alarm goes off: someone burned popcorn. Security orders everyone still inside to evacuate.
A colleague from accounting asks you to cover for her tomorrow processing expense reports. “It’s easy, you just tick boxes.”
HR wants a short video, “Why I Chose Our Company,” for career day. Due tomorrow.
right: Say you don’t have a camera

text: Legal suggests an evening course, “Law Basics for Non-Lawyers.” Upside: you’ll be able to argue with lawyers.
As you’re leaving, the boss asks: “Why isn’t your annual training plan filled out? Everyone else has done theirs.” It’s 6:05 p.m.
Accounting sends an acknowledgment form for the new accounting policy. 80 pages. Signature due by 7 p.m.
A lawyer friend calls in the evening: “Send me your employment contract — I bet there’s something illegal in it.” You’re exhausted.
HR asks you to stay late: “We need to check personnel files — you have the neatest handwriting.” 300 folders.
7:10 p.m. The team chat is buzzing with a rumor about bonus cuts. Everyone’s writing “I heard…” You actually know something.
6 p.m. HR reminds you: last day to add family to your health insurance. You need 12 documents and a copy of your marriage certificate.
The accountant writes in the evening: “Your annual tax was recalculated — you owe $41.” Payable only in cash at the cashier’s desk.
The time-management coach asks you to fill in an evening productivity journal. It takes 40 minutes.
A coworker confesses: “I’m on sick leave, but actually at the beach. If anyone asks, I’m coughing.” The boss is calling.
The boss in the evening: “Write a memo to Legal explaining why we missed the payment.” It was late because of his signature.
HR reminds you: tomorrow is the last day to confirm your vacation dates. You still haven’t picked any.
Accounting sends out a 12-page “Business Travel Paperwork Guide.” You leave tomorrow.
HR invites you to “Work-Life Balance” training at 8 p.m. Online, runs until 10.
Legal forwards you 40 emails “for your information,” all marked “important.” None contains a question.
The fire warden corners you: “You must know the evacuation plan by heart for Monday’s inspection.”
6:30 p.m. The accountant is in tears: the software deleted the bonus sheet. She asks you to help rebuild it from old emails.
The boss signed your vacation request but added: “stay reachable.” Ask what that means?
right: Quietly buy a new SIM card

text: Mom needs your income certificate for her loan application. You don’t remember where to order it.
Your Excel course certificate arrives. The name on it says “John Doe.”
A friend in HR whispers: “They want to send you on a week-long training course in another city.”
7 p.m. The accountant sends a form: “Sign for your holiday gift.” The gift is last year’s calendar.
HR invites you to a “Meet HR” evening. They promise to explain how your salary works.
6:15 p.m. Boss: “Send me the reconciliation with the contractor by 8 — Legal’s on fire.” The contractor closed at 6.
Legal wants to discuss a power of attorney: you’d sign documents on the director’s behalf.
An evening email from accounting: “Your corporate card has been blocked for a missing expense report.”
Your neighbor hears you work “in an office” and asks for help with his tax return right now.
A coworker on sick leave sends voice messages: “So how are you all coping without me? Send me what you did.” Nine of them.
HR reminds you your health certificate expires tomorrow. New ones are only issued at 8 a.m., across town.
You’ve been assigned an online productivity course: the videos can’t be sped up or skipped. 6 hours.
HR congratulates you on your work anniversary. The date is wrong — they’ve added a year.
The accountant suggests an “optimization”: pay part of your bonus as a meal allowance. Sounds fishy.
The boss in chat in the evening: “Who signed the bonus order? I don’t have a copy.” You did — at his request.
Someone drops a document into the team chat: “New Working Hours Rules,” signed by an unknown department.
9:10 a.m. Accounting says payday is delayed a day “due to a technical glitch.” Your mortgage payment is due today.
HR has rolled out digital sick notes, but still wants a paper one “for the archive.” Bring it?
Morning briefing: “How to Use Stairs Properly.” It’s in the 12th-floor meeting room, and the elevator is broken.
The boss, first thing: “I need your August vacation — take September, it’s lovely then.” Your tickets are already booked.
8:55 a.m. Legal calls: “Did you tell someone yesterday ‘it’s a deal’? That could be a verbal contract!” You were talking about lunch.
HR introduces a morning “Ready to Work” checklist: eight items, including “smiled.” Due by 9:15.
Accounting demands “original” travel tickets. They’re e-tickets. A printout isn’t an original.
HR offers to let you work remotely two days a week, but your contract says “at the location of the desk.”
9:30 a.m. Drill: the mock fire is in your office. You’ve been cast as “the victim” and must lie on the floor for an hour.
You’re enrolled in “New Managers School.” You’re not a manager — but the person with a similar name is. Go in his place?
The accountant says you were mistakenly awarded a 50-cent bonus. “No big deal, just sign the payslip.”
The boss wants your effectiveness over six months justified “in a single number” by 10 a.m. It’s for KPIs.
The office manager asks you to sign the archive key log. Your signature’s already there — from last year.
right: Ask to reuse the old one

text: The nurse at the checkup: “We’ll measure height; weight is optional.” The scale is in the middle of the hallway.
HR launches a “quiet hour” from 9 to 10 — no calls. At 9:05, HR calls to check whether you’re observing quiet hour.
HR asks why your vacation request starts on the boss’s birthday.
Accounting wants the receipt for the donuts you bought the team. The intern ate it. Literally.
right: Write it up about the intern

text: Legal: “I urgently need your signature on the supplier NDA.” The NDA forbids saying you signed an NDA.
Workplace safety checks your posture: “Back straight, feet on the floor.” You’re sitting on one leg like a heron.
Boss: “I need your goals by 11, and they must align with the team’s goals.” The team’s goals are classified.
HR hands you a new employment record book: the old one “accidentally got coffee on it.” You’re rewriting your work history by hand.
Accounting rolls out digital receipts: a photo of each, geotag and comment. You have 20 receipts today.
Team-building starts at 9 with a “trust exercise”: walk through the office blindfolded.
HR wants you to be an “internal recruiter” and bring a friend on board. The bonus comes after they’ve worked a year.
A coworker brings a pie and whispers: “Sign my training request as project lead.” You’re not the project lead.
right: Eat the pie and say no

text: HR announces a new “engagement points” system. Points are awarded for likes on the internal social network.
Accounting wants an explanation by lunch: why did you take the train instead of flying? It was cheaper.
Legal asks you to review a client email template. It mentions “company lawyer” 14 times, all misspelled.
8:40 a.m. The boss in the elevator: “You’re in charge of training, right? No? Well, now you are.” The doors close.
right: Get off at the next floor

text: HR urgently wants you to consent to a transfer to a “new legal entity.” Nobody knows what will change.
First aid is taking temperatures this morning. You’re at 99.0°F — from sprinting to the turnstile. They tell you to go home.
Accounting wants your stationery advance closed out: you bought a pen for $4.99, but the advance was $5.
HR says your team is piloting the new 360-degree review. You must rate 20 colleagues by lunch.
A morning invite: “How to Stop Procrastinating” training. The start has been postponed indefinitely.
The boss wants the vacation schedule redone “by seniority” by 10 a.m. You’re the most junior on the team.
HR asks for another passport photo for your file. The old one “got lost.” The photo studio opens at 10.
9:20 a.m. Legal asks you to rewrite your internal report without the word “problem.” The report is about a problem.
Accounting offers to pay salaries in cash “while the bank updates its system.” The cashier’s desk is in the basement; the line reaches the elevator.
Workplace safety puts up a new sign: “Caution: Slippery Floor.” Right next to your desk.
right: Use it as a coat rack

text: A coworker asks you to sign a “collective letter” for a pay raise. So far it has one signature — his.
HR declares “Health Week”: morning exercises in the lobby at 8:45. Skipping costs you points.
Accounting calls: “Why haven’t you picked up your payslip?” Payslips are now only in an app that won’t open.
The boss wants an HR profile on a new hire. The hire hasn’t been hired yet; the profile is due today.
HR asks for a name for the new engagement survey. You suggest “Survey.” It’s rejected as “not inclusive.”
Legal advises saving all work emails to a separate folder, “just in case.” There are 18,000 of them.
HR offers a “voluntary” switch to a shorter workweek. The salary gets shorter too. Think it over?
A colleague from Legal asks you to proofread a lawsuit. It’s against your supplier — who’s a friend.
The fire inspector finds a space heater in your office and demands you “surrender it immediately.” It’s 40°F outside.
The accountant asks you to fill in a spreadsheet of the quarter’s coffee spending. The whole team bought coffee, but the spreadsheet is yours.
Training asks you to be an “expert” and record a lesson for newbies. Camera and lights — in the kitchen at 3 p.m.
After the engagement survey, HR is gathering a “focus group of the dissatisfied.” You were invited based on your “anonymous” answers.
Boss: “Sign the write-off for this laptop.” It’s your work laptop — and you’re using it right now.
left: Sign and wait for a new one

text: 2:30 p.m. Accounting wants you at the other office to sign for your vacation pay. “Can’t do it electronically, it’s money.”
Legal suggests renaming your project: “Breakthrough” sounds like a promise. They propose “Attempt.”
HR introduces shift work for a team that’s never worked shifts. Your shift: noon to 9 p.m.
HR says you have a “low corporate life participation index.” They recommend joining at least one club.
A coworker asks you to attend teamwork training in his place. “Nobody checks who’s who anyway.”
The accountant asks why your business trip shows four lunches a day. You were crossing time zones.
The boss wants you to take the corporate values quiz. He scored 40% and would rather you didn’t beat him.
First aid invites you to a full checkup: six rooms on three floors, all during your lunch break.
Legal wants you to confirm “for the record” that you’ve never discussed salaries with colleagues. You did — yesterday.
HR offers to “voluntarily” roll your unused vacation into next year. The “voluntary” box is already ticked.
HR launches a “recognition wall”: everyone thanks a colleague with a sticky note. You thank the coffee machine.
Accounting will reimburse gym costs if you show your membership and “a photo from a workout.”
The team chat is arguing over who’s responsible for the safety briefing log. It turned up in your drawer.
right: Hand it to the office manager
